notes:
A shorter name for the export
Export the KPI page

entries.title: A shorter name for the export
entries.detail: Export now names its file like pactum_KPIs-ISGs_20261119.html, with today's date as year, month and day. Files of several days sort by date.

entries.title: Export the KPI page
entries.detail: A new Export button stands first in the top bar. It saves one file with the KPIs ISGs and Settings › About pactum. Open it in any browser: the hovers, sorting, ISG buttons and switches all work, but nothing can be entered or saved. It holds your figures, so give it only to people who may see them.

entries.title: How far ID and the team are apart
entries.detail: In the 2×2 chart, a thin vertical bar now runs from Maturity Ø ID to Maturity Ø ISG. The bubble sits at its middle. A long bar means ID and the ISG team rate the maturity quite differently. Point at the bubble to see both values. The selected ISG's bar is amber.

entries.title: One maturity for one ISG
entries.detail: When you show one ISG with its button, its row has one column "Maturity Ø" in place of "Maturity Ø ID" and "Maturity Ø ISG". It is the mean of the two, as in the 2×2. Its hover shows both. The overview of all ISGs keeps both columns.

entries.title: The ID ISGs rate themselves too
entries.detail: In Data ISGs, the table "Filled by the ISG teams" now has the 8 ID ISGs too, first, as in ID's table. Their levels start as ID's levels. Change them, and only Maturity Ø ISG changes, not Maturity Ø ID.

entries.title: Anonymize only in one ISG's view
entries.detail: The switch "Anonymize" now works only when you press an ISG's button. Then the 2×2 chart shows only that ISG's name. When you press a row in the table, every bubble keeps its name.

entries.title: Anonymize keeps all names until you select
entries.detail: With the switch "Anonymize" on and no ISG selected, every bubble in the 2×2 chart now has its name. Select an ISG, and only that ISG keeps its name.

entries.title: Anonymize the 2×2
entries.detail: A new switch "Anonymize" stands after the other switches. It is off at first: every ISG in the 2×2 chart has its name. Turn it on, and only the selected ISG keeps its name, also when you point at its bubble. With no ISG selected, no bubble has a name. It stays as you set it when you change the view or the ISG.

entries.title: The 2×2 switch on every page
entries.detail: The switch "Efficiency and maturity" is now always there, after the other switches. Turn it off, and the 2×2 chart goes away on the page of all ISGs and in the view of one ISG. It stays as you set it when you change the view or the ISG.

entries.title: One ISG without the 2×2
entries.detail: When you press one ISG's button, a new switch "Efficiency and maturity" stands after the other switches. Turn it off, and the 2×2 chart goes away: you see the ISG's row and its spiders with figures. It stays off for the next ISG you press. The page of all ISGs always shows the 2×2.

entries.title: Only pactum reads your data
entries.detail: pactum's server now gives your data only to pactum's own window, and to a browser that you open with Open in Browser. Other programs on this Mac get no data from it.

entries.title: Safer, and faster to start
entries.detail: pactum reads your files in about two thirds of the time it took. Its page now runs only its own code, and no other web page can show it inside itself or read from it. The app carries Node 24.22.3, with Node's security fixes of November.

entries.title: The Field Manual is up to date
entries.detail: Docs opens the fixed Field Manual: no complexity factor, the two minimums as petrol lines, the maturity spider as the average of the ID's and the ISG team's levels, and the Minimum Viable Efficiency as six standings from 1 to 5.

entries.title: Spiders the same size in both views
entries.detail: The spiders are 390 px, with all ISGs and with one ISG picked alike, so an ISG looks the same in both views.

entries.title: Figures as tall as the spiders
entries.detail: When you pick one ISG with its button, the figures beside its spiders are as tall as the spiders' card.

entries.title: Spiders in between, and one ISG laid out anew
entries.detail: The spiders are a size in between: at most 480 px, not as big as in build 85. When you pick one ISG with its button, the efficiency and maturity chart takes the whole width, and the figures stand to the right of its spiders.

entries.title: Bigger spiders, each with its own labels
entries.detail: The two spiders of each ISG now fill the width of its card. Under each spider is one row of labels, each with its line: its mean, the Average ID CxS with its value for that spider, and its minimum. The legend beside the spiders and its sentence about the area are gone.

entries.title: One maturity in the spiders, and no complexity factor
entries.detail: Each maturity spider draws one shape: the average of the ID's level and the ISG team's level in each dimension. Under it is one "Maturity Ø", like the "Efficiency Ø" under the other spider. The complexity factor is gone from the KPI page and from Data ISGs. The factors you entered stay in your file.

entries.title: Names closer to their bubbles
entries.detail: In the efficiency and maturity chart, a name now tries every 45° round its bubble, the four corners too, before it moves a line or more away. So more names stand right beside their bubble.

entries.title: No lines from names to bubbles
entries.detail: In the efficiency and maturity chart, a name that stands a line or more away from its bubble no longer has a thin line to it. Every name keeps its place, and no name covers another or a bubble.

entries.title: Each spider label says its mean
entries.detail: The labels of the spiders say the mean of their line: Maturity by the ID, Maturity by the ISG team, the Average ID CxS (for the efficiency and the maturity) and both minimums under their spiders. A line without values has no mean.

entries.title: Maturity by the ID is back in the legend
entries.detail: The spiders' legend names "Maturity by the ID" again, with its line in amber on every card, as the spiders are.

entries.title: Every spider in amber
entries.detail: Every ISG's spiders are amber now, not only the selected one's: the efficiency, the maturity by ID and the maturity by the ISG team, and the three means under them. The selected ISG still shows by its card's amber ground and edge. The legend no longer names "Maturity by the ID".

entries.title: Petrol minimums, and maturity from both sides
entries.detail: The Minimum Viable Efficiency and Maturity are petrol now, in the 2×2 and in the spiders, so they stand apart from the selected ISG's amber. The corner where both are met has a soft petrol ground. In the 2×2, an ISG's maturity is the mean of Maturity Ø ID and Maturity Ø ISG, and its hover shows both. The axes are named as the overview's columns.

entries.title: An update no longer freezes pactum
entries.detail: When pactum installed an update, it could stop at "Installing". Then About, Docs and Quit did nothing, while the page still worked. Now pactum quits within 3 seconds, and the update goes on.

entries.title: pactum trusts only its own server
entries.detail: pactum shows only pages from the server it started itself. Before, another program on this Mac that took pactum's port first could have shown its pages in pactum's window. Now pactum shows why instead, and opens nothing in the browser.

entries.title: Safer and faster
entries.detail: pactum starts faster: it reads your files in about half the time. Its server keeps running after a bad request, and a save that fails now says "not saved" instead of stopping pactum. It is built with Node's newest security fixes.

entries.title: A Minimum Viable Efficiency for each efficiency KPI
entries.detail: Data ISGs has a Minimum Viable Efficiency for each of the six efficiency KPIs, with the same selectors as the Minimum Viable Maturity. Your one value became each KPI's. Each efficiency spider draws them in amber, with the name under that spider; the Minimum Viable Maturity's name stands under the maturity spider. The 2×2 draws their mean. A switch Minimum Viable Efficiency, left of Minimum Viable Maturity, shows or hides it.

entries.title: A softer amber for the selected ISG
entries.detail: The amber behind the selected ISG's row, its figures and its spiders is softer, and so is the amber area in its spiders, like the cross-hatch in the 2×2.

entries.title: Both minimums at the top of Data ISGs
entries.detail: Data ISGs starts with Minimum Viable: the Minimum Viable Efficiency, then the Minimum Viable Maturity, in a section of their own. The cross-hatch in the 2×2 is softer. Docs, the Field Manual, names today's pages and says your data is in iCloud.

entries.title: Minimum Viable Maturity and Minimum Viable Efficiency
entries.detail: The Minimum Viable Standard is now called Minimum Viable Maturity. Data ISGs has a new part, Efficiency ISGs: enter the Minimum Viable Efficiency, 0 to 5. The 2×2 draws it as an amber line up the chart, and cross-hatches the corner where an ISG meets both minimums. Docs, the Field Manual, says so too.

entries.title: Minimum Viable Standard
entries.detail: The Accepted Minimum is now called Minimum Viable Standard: on the switch, in the legends of the spiders and the 2×2, and in the table under Data ISGs. Your values stay as they were.

entries.title: Accepted Minimum in the 2×2, whole names on the buttons
entries.detail: The 2×2 draws the Accepted Minimum as an amber line at the mean of its levels, as in the spiders, with a legend under it. The ISG buttons show whole names, such as ID ISG D-BAUG and ISG D-ARCH. The note under the overview no longer points to the KPIs without data.

entries.title: Arrows on every column
entries.detail: Every column title in the overview shows two small arrows, so you see that it sorts. A sorted title keeps only one: up when the lowest is first, down when the highest is first.

entries.title: Sort the overview
entries.detail: Click a column's title in the overview to sort all ISGs by it, the best first. Click again to turn the order round, and a third time to go back. The table is one list now, without the rows "ID ISGs" and "Departmental ISGs"; without a click, the order is as before.

entries.title: No hover left behind
entries.detail: A scroll now closes every hover. Before, a hover of the 2×2 could stay on the page after a scroll with the trackpad, far from its bubble.

entries.title: Calm hovers
entries.detail: Every hover now looks the same: the ISG, what is shown, one value, then labels and numbers in straight columns and a short note, in one size of text. The spiders' hover shows the KPIs and the nine levels as two small tables.

entries.title: Nothing typed is lost when pactum quits, and a clear hover
entries.detail: Before pactum quits, for an update too, it saves what you are typing under Data ISGs. In the overview, the hover shows the ISG, the KPI under it, the value, and then the median, the standing and the two figures behind it in two straight columns, without file names.

entries.title: Bigger spiders, cleaner figures and names
entries.detail: The spiders are bigger and use the card's room, with the legend beside them. The specifics stay in the figures, not between the spiders. The figures show names and numbers only; point at a row to see its file. In the 2×2, every name sits right beside its bubble: names are measured, not guessed, so ID ISG D-BIOL no longer goes a line up.

entries.title: Whole specifics, readable names
entries.detail: Under Specifics ISGs, each field is as tall as its text, so long points are no longer cut off. In the 2×2, a picked ISG's name stays where it was, so it no longer lies on a neighbour's name (ISG D-INFK and ISG D-HEST).
